status: Active implementation; not deployed or enabled on main yet
requirements: A push to main starts validation, version preparation, client/server/UI packaging and scoped deployment without manual workflow dispatch.
An explicit numeric release tag starts the same pipeline with that version, after checking source/version agreement.
Default GitHub retention is latest stable release and version tag only; remove superseded unprotected previews.
Preserve versions only when the user explicitly requests retention; record exact tags in PORTHUB_RETAIN_TAGS.
Keep unchanged Rust modules/dependencies and the independently built terminal runtime cached. Do not mix incompatible binaries or reuse a version for different published contents.
Use built-in failed-job reruns for transient errors on unchanged source; source-changing fixes rebuild affected code and relink.
Publish only a fully validated consistent ten-platform bundle; keep the previous latest release if validation fails.
Scope deployments to PortHub services and agents, preserve unrelated machines/workloads and keep rollback evidence.

implemented.retention: Protected tag/release allowlist and unprotected draft/prerelease cleanup wired into the existing publisher. Source reachability and latest-release checks retained. Eleven tests pass; live dry run against v1.8.9 proposes no deletion.
implemented.cache: Independent helper builds cached immediately after completion and before downstream Rust tests; workspace Rust crate/dependency cache retained.
implemented.version_preparation: scripts/prepare-release.py is implemented, dry-run by default. Default-branch source can advance a previously published patch version using a bot commit that changes only Cargo.toml and the matching workspace Cargo.lock entries. Explicit numeric tags must match committed workspace versions. It rejects dirty/mismatched source and downgrades, verifies latest-source ancestry, skips superseded default-branch runs and recognizes already-published source. Eight tests pass against real isolated local Git repositories and bare remotes; no production branch was changed. Now skips drafts/tags reserved by different source; matching same-source drafts remain resumable. Eleven real-Git tests pass.
implemented.build_orchestration: Continuous release workflow now defines main-push/numeric-tag entry points, automatic version preparation and reusable client/server builds pinned to its prepared revision. Manual verify-only mode avoids release mutations. Client aggregation collects only the ten platform directories and validates all thirty assets, avoiding collisions with server artifacts in the shared run. Server artifacts include API, edge, runtime and firewall. Actionlint 1.7.12 accepts all three workflow definitions; version tests (8), retention tests (11) and offline native preflight/collector tests (20) pass.
implemented.publication: scripts/publish-release.py validates all thirty local assets and uploaded GitHub SHA256 digests before promotion; it can resume matching drafts and never overwrite published assets. Ten tests pass; wired into the existing manual publisher. Final automatic deployment/publication gate remains pending.
implemented.server_packaging: Server workflow now packages core, edge and firewall images from the pinned, checksum-verified native binary artifact without another Rust build. It checks image revision, role UID/GID and all role/runtime help commands with network disabled and capabilities dropped, then saves checksummed image archives. Initial GitHub verification pending. Verified on GitHub run 41231567603 at source 2cdee21d7b07b88002d7a984ae3571fc2e028a1c: ARM64 build and all three image smoke tests pass, image archive artifact 187763285 bytes. No image was deployed.

remaining: Validate the orchestrated workflow on GitHub and complete all platform gates before enabling it on main.

Dedicated narrowly scoped production CI deployment credentials; repository currently has no deployment secrets.
Add final publication and deployment gates to the orchestrator and test the full path before declaring push-to-deploy live.
